The must-sees

10 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Neighbourhood

    Barrio Santa Cruz

    This was the city’s Jewish quarter until the violence of 1391 and the expulsion of 1492. Its lanes were tidied and romanticised in the early 20th century.

    Look for

    The Callejón del Agua runs along the Alcázar’s garden wall, which once carried water pipes for the palace.

  2. 02
    Landmark · 1198

    Giralda

    It was finished in 1198 as the minaret of the mosque, and ramps instead of stairs lead to the top. In the 16th century Hernán Ruiz added the belfry and the bronze weathervane, the Giraldillo.

    Look for

    On each face of the Almohad shaft, find the sebka: a lattice of diamond-shaped brick panels.

  3. 03
    Park

    María Luisa Park

    The Infanta María Luisa gave most of her palace gardens to the city in 1893. Jean-Claude Forestier redesigned them for the 1929 Exposition.

    Look for

    Find the monument to the poet Bécquer: his bust above three marble women round a tree, showing the stages of love.

  4. 04
    Building · 2011

    Metropol Parasol

    Locals call it Las Setas, the mushrooms, and it was designed by Jürgen Mayer. Roman remains found during construction are shown in a museum underneath.

    Look for

    Under the canopy, at street level, the Encarnación market still sells fish, meat and vegetables.

  5. 05
    Square · 1929

    Plaza de España

    Aníbal González designed it for the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition. Tiled alcoves along the wall represent the provinces of Spain.

    Look for

    The four bridges over the canal stand for the old kingdoms of Spain, with blue and white ceramic balustrades.

  6. 06
    Venue

    Real Maestranza Bullring

    Construction began in 1749 and took more than a century to complete. It belongs to an old noble riding brotherhood and includes a museum.

    Look for

    The Puerta del Príncipe is the gate through which a matador is carried shoulder-high after a great afternoon.

  7. 07
    Palace

    Royal Alcázar

    Its core is the Mudéjar palace Pedro I had built in the 1360s by craftsmen from Granada and Toledo. The upper floors are still used by the Spanish royal family when in Seville.

    Look for

    Over the Lion Gate, the entrance, a tiled heraldic lion holds a cross in its paw.

  8. 08
    Church · 1506

    Seville Cathedral

    It was built from 1434 on the site of the city’s great mosque, keeping the minaret and the orange-tree courtyard. A monumental tomb inside holds remains attributed to Christopher Columbus.

    Look for

    At Columbus’s tomb the coffin rides on the shoulders of four heralds, for the kingdoms of Castile, León, Aragon and Navarre.

  9. 09
    Fortress

    Torre del Oro

    It was built in the early 13th century to guard the river, and a chain could be stretched from it to the far bank. Today it holds a small naval museum.

    Look for

    Notice the three tiers: the twelve-sided base is Almohad, while the small round top was added in 1760.

  10. 10
    Neighbourhood

    Triana

    For centuries Triana supplied the tiles that decorate Seville. Many of the sailors on the voyages to the Americas came from these streets.

    Look for

    At the Triana end of the bridge, the small tiled Capillita del Carmen is nicknamed the lighter for its shape.
